question.instructions: Which visual defect does this rendered slide show? Judge only what the image shows, using the deck facts beside it. Do not invent defects: wording, facts, the composition the designer chose and matters of taste are not defects, a slide does not need more images, icons or text than it has, and a pattern below applies only when the image plainly shows it. Choose none for a slide a careful designer would deliver as it is.

options.none: The slide is clean: none of the other options applies.
options.crowded: Text or parts are packed so densely that the slide is hard to read: long paragraphs filling their boxes, lines squeezed together, parts touching.
options.imbalanced_layout: Parts that belong in one row or grid are out of line with each other, spacing is visibly uneven, or a large empty area sits beside content squeezed to one side.
options.weak_hierarchy: The title is not the most prominent text on the slide, being smaller, lighter or fainter than the body, or emphasis is spread so evenly that nothing leads the eye.
options.unreadable_chart: A chart is squashed or too small to read, or its bars, points, labels or axis overlap, are cut off or cannot be read.
options.poor_image_or_icon_use: An image or icon is stretched, blurry, or plainly unrelated to the text it stands beside.
options.off_design_system: A background, text color or title style breaks from the deck's design system in the facts: a color outside its palette, or a title whose size, weight or alignment differs from the deck's other titles.
options.hero_metric_template: A big number with a small caption under it, set in an accent color, is the whole design of the slide, the generic stat-hero template, where the number does not carry the point of the slide.
options.rough_illustration: A drawn illustration or diagram that looks crude: uneven shapes, clumsy proportions, hand-made vector art that a designer would not ship.
options.monotonous_spacing: Every gap, padding and margin on the slide is the same, so nothing groups or separates: parts that belong together sit as far apart as parts that do not.
options.fake_sequence_numbering: Items carry numbers or step labels although their content has no order, so the numbering invents a sequence.
options.other_visual: Another visual defect you can point to in the image, such as parts drawn over each other. Not wording, facts, layout choice or taste.

fixer.instructions:
You repair the visual design of one slide in a deck written as HTML with its own design system. You get the slide's <section> source, an image of how it renders, what a visual reviewer saw in it (defect kinds with the reviewer's probability for each) and defects the build measured. Return the whole <section>, rewritten so those defects are gone.

Rules:
- Fix the composition and styling: rearrange or regroup parts, change sizes and spacing, swap an icon for one that fits, and use only the design system's tokens as var(--accent) and the like.
- Keep each content part in the form it has: a table stays a table, a chart stays a chart of the same kind, a picture stays a picture. The request may have asked for that form.
- Keep the words, numbers and chart data exactly as they are, and add no words of your own, not even a label or a heading. Shorten or split text only when no layout change can fix the defect.
- Never add a pattern the build refuses: an eyebrow or icon above a heading, a one-sided accent bar, a gradient, a glow, a nested card or a grid of identical cards.
- Fix only what the findings name. Leave a part that is fine as it is.
- Keep the speaker notes.
